title: Musike: an open-source music player with nothing to sell you

facts.method: tool's own README and repo page, read on the day of the plan
facts.limits: It is for personal use: the README says playing YouTube streams without ads breaks YouTube's terms, and public bots like Groovy and Rythm were shut down after notices from Google.

verify_before_render: Every point cites its source in the plan (repo-musike-01/plan.json).
Kit images are drawn from the plan's own visual spec only.

scenes.heading: MUSIKE SELLS YOU NOTHING
scenes.say: What if your music app had no ads, no account, and nothing left to sell you?

scenes.heading: IT FETCHES THE STREAM ITSELF
scenes.say: A small server that you run fetches the stream itself and hands it to the player — that is why there is nothing to skip.

scenes.heading: AUDIO BECOMES VIDEO MID-SONG
scenes.say: Flip between audio and video mid-song, from the same second — for songs it even finds the artist's official music video.

scenes.heading: ONE PLAYER, EVERY SCREEN
scenes.say: Desktop, phone, TV, browser, Docker — the same player runs on all of them, and the phone app needs no computer.

scenes.heading: YOUR LIBRARY IS A FILE
nodes: Library lives in a local file
Load it on any other Musike
scenes.say: Your playlists and favourites stay in a local file you can export — take your whole library to any other install.

scenes.heading: THE CATCH
nodes: Groovy and Rythm were shut down

youtube.title: Musike Runs on 8 Platforms and Charges Nothing
youtube.description: Musike is an open-source music player for YouTube's catalog. A server you run fetches the stream with yt-dlp, so playback has no ads, no account and no subscription. Audio and video switch mid-track, it runs on Windows, macOS, Linux, Android, Android TV, iPhone, as a browser PWA and in Docker, and your playlists and favourites live in a local file you can export. Personal use only — the README's legal notice explains YouTube's terms. Repo: https://github.com/Ernani1234/musike #Shorts #Musike #OpenSource #MusicPlayer #SelfHosted

idea: Musike plays YouTube's catalog with no ads, account or subscription because a server you run fetches the stream; it switches audio to video mid-song, runs on every screen, and keeps your library in a file you own.

claims.text: A server you run fetches the stream with yt-dlp and hands the bytes to the player.
Audio and video switch mid-track from the same position, and songs get the artist's official music video.
It runs as Windows, macOS and Linux apps, Android, Android TV and iPhone apps, an installable browser PWA, and a Docker image.
Playlists and favorites live in a local file you can export and move to any other Musike.
